turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through. I'll grab your obs while he's still stuck on the phone. Jacket can stay on.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ta. Sorry, the Monash was a car park. I nearly turned around and went back to the office.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): It's been like that all morning. Blood pressure's one thirty-two over seventy-eight, pulse is fifty-eight, and the scales say eighty-six point four kilos.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Eighty-six? I was under eighty last time I bothered. Couldn't tell you when. I'm not fussed, honestly.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put that in the chart. There's water on the bench if you want it. He won't be long.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, sorry. This thing's been spinning since nine. What's brought you in, then?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Probably nothing. I've been a bit tired. Work's flat out and I'm fifty-two, so I reckon that's the whole story.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tired like you could sleep, or tired like there's no petrol in the tank?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No petrol. I still get through the day. I'm not dropping off in meetings or anything dramatic.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long's that been?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, months. Since last winter. Well, actually, it might've been the winter before. I can't keep the years straight.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, I've clicked the wrong patient. Say the timing again?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know the date. Last winter, or the one before. A good few months. It's been much the same, so I left it.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): And you're putting the whole thing on work.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Work and being fifty-two, yeah. I do the accounts at Knox council. Late ones most nights. Anyone would be wiped.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Knox, right. Are you feeling the cold, or is it just this room?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): This room's fine. I am a bit cold, even at home with the heater going. I blamed the office aircon for ages, but it's not only there. Still, it's nothing.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a box just popped up over your notes. Cold at home, did you say?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Heater on, and I still feel it. It's mild. I'm not wrapped in a doona or anything.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): The nurse has you at eighty-six point four. Have you actually put weight on?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, yeah. I was under eighty whenever I last stood on a scale, a couple of years back or longer, and I never wrote it down. Desk job and biscuits in the tearoom. Hardly an illness.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are the bowels doing?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit sluggish. Every second day, and sometimes I skip two. I wasn't even going to mention it.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the bowl, or black stools?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. They're just slow. I eat fine, before you ask.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mood. Are you flat, or is this only the energy?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a bit flat, if you want it straight. Not depressed, not crying in the car. Just over the job and getting older. I still front up.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Flat, and you reckon it's the job. Any thyroid problems in the family, while this page thinks about loading?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Mum had an underactive thyroid, little tablets for years. She's gone now, so I can't ask her the name of them. Don't make a big thing of it, she was old.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did anyone ever check yours?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Once, yeah. They said it was borderline. I was meant to repeat it and I didn't, because I felt fine.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline. Was there a number, a TSH, anything?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No number that I remember. Just borderline, they said, and the letter's long gone. Last winter, or the winter before. Same muddle as the tiredness.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm in the results tab and I can't see a thyroid test on this file at all. Somewhere else?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Might've been the bulk-billing clinic in Bayswater. Or before I started coming here. I didn't keep it. They weren't worried, so I wasn't.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Righto. And it's frozen again. Of course. Did that Monash mess get you the whole way in?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Stopped dead back to the Springvale exit. A ute into the barrier, everyone slowing down for a stickybeak.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): I thought I was clever coming Burwood Road. Still took forty minutes from Box Hill. Should've been fifteen.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): At least the sun's out. Had the cricket on the radio. They're getting flogged, can't bat to save themselves.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I stayed up for the first session like a dill. Slips dropped three catches. There goes the weekend and it's only Tuesday.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): My brother-in-law texted a rant about the selectors before I'd had a coffee. I didn't even reply. Whole summer down the drain if this keeps up.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah, don't get me started. Alright, cursor's back. Your hair. Is it coming out in the shower more than it used to?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Same as ever. Thin on top since my thirties, nothing new. I'm not shedding.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chin up a bit, I'll feel your neck. Still half an eye on this login, sorry.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Go on, then. You'll say my hands are cold. I already told you.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): No goitre. The thyroid isn't enlarged. Hands are cool, yeah, but nothing dramatic on a quick feel.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): So that's it? I've got to be back before one.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not quite. Cold, tired, weight up, slow bowels, and your mum had an underactive thyroid. This could be an underactive thyroid, a working idea, not a label. It might still just be the job and your age, and I can't split them from here.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. Feels like a lot of fuss for being a bit off.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll do a blood test, thyroid function. I want an actual number, not a memory of someone saying borderline. Pathology downstairs can take it today if you've got ten minutes.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I've got something at two. If it's quick, I'll do it today. I don't want another bit of paper living in the car.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's quick. I'll add a full blood count on the same form, only because we're already taking blood. Not because I've thought of some other disease.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. And I'm not going on some mad diet, if that's the next speech.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't. No crash diet, and don't buy thyroid tablets or kelp from the chemist while we wait. Come back in two weeks and we'll go through whatever comes back.
[SEG0055] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the form and walk you down if you like. Two tubes and you're done.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Prior thyroid test is recalled as borderline and absent from current file, but status completed is only patient-reported, not confirmed.
bad.text: thyroid function test (type=laboratory, status=completed, indication=Patient recalls being told the result was borderline, with no number remembered; not found on the current file)

omissions.text: Hair loss was recorded incorrectly: the patient denied any new hair loss or increased shedding, saying thinning on top has been present since his thirties and is nothing new.
Past history of a previous thyroid test being 'borderline' with repeat testing advised but not done is missing from medical history/plan context.

The planned thyroid function test is recorded as 'completed' for the prior test, but the doctor explicitly said there was no thyroid test visible on the current file and the prior test may have been done elsewhere (bulk-billing clinic in Bayswater or before attending this practice).
